Banana Pepper - portable desktop distribution

Copy this entire folder to a writable location before using it. Keep the
banana-pepper.dist marker beside the desktop executable. Start arcade-desktop
(arcade-desktop.exe on Windows), then select your own game folder or ZArchive
in the workbench. arcade-zar is the standalone archive converter.

Folder layout:
  arcade-desktop[.exe]   Workbench
  arcade-zar[.exe]       ZArchive converter
  helpers/              Compiled Water/session/game hosts and card utility
  adapters/             Guest libraries, separated by platform/architecture
  docs/                 Per-game setup and compatibility notes
  settings.cfg          Fresh default graphics, audio and input settings
  controls.cfg          Fresh default control bindings
  manifest.json         Version, platform, file sizes and SHA-256 checksums

No Rust compiler, Cargo, just or source checkout is needed for native Windows
launches. Windows x86-64 and an OpenGL-capable graphics driver are required.
Big Buck uses helpers/water-buck.exe; Ford uses its adapter in adapters/.
Other titles/backends retain the requirements and limits described in docs/.

WSL is optional and is not built by the native Windows recipe. It requires a
separately installed WSL2/WSLg Linux environment and Linux guest components.
Build the optional WSL components with just build-wsl on the build machine;
they are included in the next package as helpers/linux/banana-game-host,
helpers/linux/banana-session and the corresponding Linux adapters.
The recipient needs WSL2/WSLg and the game's Linux libraries, but no Rust
toolchain or interpreter. Linux helpers require a distro compatible with their
build environment, including glibc. Minecraft also requires the Linux adapter
adapters/linux-x86_64/libarcade_minecraft_io.so, runtime libraries and your own
captured records as described in docs/minecraft-windows.md. These files are
not silently copied from a developer's local runtime or private data.

Linux packages require desktop graphics libraries, Bubblewrap and
the 32-bit libraries required by the selected game. Wine/DXVK are needed for
Windows titles. Xvfb and diagnostic tools are needed by probe modes. Run
helpers/linux/banana-session --setup-legacy32 . to prepare the local legacy
libraries; see docs/ for package prerequisites. Third-party runtime
libraries are obtained separately and are not bundled from local caches.

All registered game launchers and session management are compiled Rust.
There is no scripts folder and no Python or shell runtime dependency.
Use helpers/banana-minecraft-card CODE PLAYER to scan a card during a running
Minecraft session (add .exe on Windows).

Settings, runtime copies, logs, saves and extracted archives are written into
this folder (runtime/ is created when needed). The library list and theme are
saved in your user configuration directory. Original game files stay separate.
Use arcade-desktop --runtime-info to inspect the resolved runtime paths.

This folder contains no games, cabinet records, captured seeds, saves, local
preferences, third-party loaders or cached third-party libraries.

Build output under target/dist is regenerated by just build. Use a separate
copy of the distribution for play; rebuilding replaces the generated folder.
